verdict.rationale: Snowflake's first-party Time Travel docs say users can query past data that has since been updated or deleted at any point within a defined period, and can restore deleted objects such as tables, or all objects in a container. That covers both halves of the story. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of restoring a corrupted (as opposed to dropped) table to a prior state, details of the retention-period limits and the as-of query syntax, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can time-travel — query data as of a past point and restore dropped or corrupted tables from history

citations.quote: Snowflake Time Travel enables accessing historical data (that is, data that has been changed or deleted) at any point within a defined period.
Query data in the past that has since been updated or deleted.
You can restore individual objects, such as tables, or restore all the objects inside a container object
